title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 11–13). L is a partially ordered set that is directed both upwards and downwards, considered only up to reversal of the order (a 'biordered' structure; the page leans on p.11's 'binaire'/'biordonnée'). The ternary relation R(a,b,c) means 'b is strictly between a and c', i.e. a<b<c or c<b<a. The goal of p.11's Lemma is to show that R determines the structure: the order is recovered from R once an orientation is fixed.

Step 1 (p.11). Comparability is recovered from R. Call a, b 'disjoint' when they are distinct and comparable. Under the divisibility (density) hypothesis on binaries, a and b are disjoint iff some c is strictly between them. This yields a comparable distinct pair to use as an 'origin', provided L has more than one point.

Step 2 (this page). Choose an ordered origin pair (a,b) of comparable distinct elements, and fix the one of the two mutually opposite orders in which a<b. The claim is that this order is entirely determined by the couple (a,b) together with R. Three sets are definable from R:
- L_{≥b} = {x : x=b or R(a,b,x)};
- L_{≤a} = {x : x=a or R(b,a,x)};
- ]a,b[ = {x : R(a,x,b)}.
Since a<b, 'a strictly between b and x' forces x<a, so L_{≤a} = {x ≤ a}; dually L_{≥b} = {x ≥ b}.

Step 3. The order itself is defined by: u ≤ v iff there exist x ∈ L_{≤a} and y ∈ L_{≥b} such that x ≤ u ≤ v ≤ y.
- Necessity uses two-sided directedness. Take a common lower bound x of u and a, and a common upper bound y of v and b. Then x ∈ L_{≤a} and y ∈ L_{≥b}.
- Sufficiency is trivial.
- Note that x < y automatically (x ≤ a < b ≤ y).

Step 4. The chain x ≤ u ≤ v ≤ y is rewritten purely in terms of betweenness: u, v are between x and y; u is between x and v; v is between u and y. This makes ≤ R-definable from (a,b).

Step 5 (p.13). The remaining lemma: if x<y, u and v are between x and y, and u is between x and v (or v between u and y), then x ≤ u ≤ v ≤ y. Its proof uses that a finite comparable configuration is a chain.

Conclusion. A directed, 'divisible' poset is determined up to duality by its strict betweenness relation, and the choice of an ordered comparable pair fixes the orientation.
errors: 'entre' must be read as non-strict betweenness (u=x, u=v, v=y allowed) in the final characterization, while R on p.11 is strict betweenness; this is never made explicit. As written with strict R, cases like u=x or u=v would be wrongly excluded.

That L_{≤a} = {x ≤ a} implicitly uses that a<b is the chosen orientation. Fine, but the definitions are only R-definable once the unordered comparable pair is known, which needs the density hypothesis of p.11.
Minor: p.13 says 'trois éléments' for x, y, u, v (four elements).

ideas.what: Recovering a (directed) partial order up to duality from its strict betweenness relation, fixing orientation by an ordered comparable pair
ideas.modern_name: order-betweenness / reconstruction of an order from betweenness
ideas.usually_credited_to: Huntington & Kline (1917) for linear orders; Pitcher–Smiley (1942), Altwegg (1950), Sholander (1952) for partial orders and lattices; later Lihová (strict order-betweenness)

ideas.what: Defining half-lines L_{≥b}, L_{≤a} and the open interval ]a,b[ from betweenness relative to an origin pair
ideas.modern_name: rays/intervals in betweenness geometry (Pasch/Hilbert ordering axioms)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but classical step: an order up to reversal is recovered from betweenness via an origin pair and two-sided directedness. This is standard in betweenness theory since Huntington, Pasch and Sholander. It is interesting only as part of Grothendieck's 1986 'réseaux via découpages' axiomatics, not as new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Line 3–4: 'la relation d'ordre définie dans les branches' is doubtful; the handwriting looks more like 'définie par les binaires' / 'des binaires' (consistent with 'L binaire' on p.11).
Margin bracket reads 'déterminés par R' (the three sets are R-definable), correctly placed.
'Il faut et il suffit' line is correct; '[-x∈-]' before 'x,y∈L' is a struck-out start.
In 'L_{≥b}' the struck text above reads like '[-x≥b ou-]' replaced by 'x=b ou', as transcribed.
